correctness.rationale: The support digraph is exhaustively constructed for every labeling and opinion coloring through order five and checked by two independent transition algorithms. Two unrelated terminal-SCC algorithms agree for each case. Graph isomorphism canonicalization proves the complete three-class five-vertex census; direct neighbor-count witnesses and a parameter-free strict-majority leaf construction prove existence at every higher order. All quantifiers and the connected n>=2 boundary are explicit; no finite experiment stands in for the infinite existence proof.

value.rationale: The smallest connected network permitting perpetual random-majority tie activity, rather than merely transient coin flips, is a model-structural threshold. Identifying all minimal graph types (and exact labeled incidence) answers a motivated characterization left open by the general absorbing-state literature. The three types share a previously unisolated protected two-phase deterministic backbone and one persistent random degree-even vertex; the bull construction makes the mechanism universal for every larger order, yielding a useful finite exact benchmark.
